items.body: Credit: Samsung China TL;DR Samsung has confirmed that it will launch a new foldable in China next week, hinting at the W27. This will likely be a China-only variant of the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, featuring a more premium design with a gold-colored frame. A tipster has also posted a picture of the Samsung W27 while claiming it will have the same specs as the Z Fold 8 Ultra. Samsung has already launched three foldable phones this year, namely the Galaxy Z Flip 8, Galaxy Z Fold 8 , and Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra . items.title: LISA Is Dressed to Kill in Action-Packed ‘Tarantino’ Music Video: Watch
items.summary: Directed by James Mackel, the visual is three-and-a-half minutes of spy stuff, as LISA makes short work of the many villains who lurk in her hotel.
items.body: Quentin Tarantino, your new action star is here. And her name is LISA . The BLACKPINK icon stars in the music video for “Tarantino,” which arrived at the stroke of midnight along with the release of her new six-track collection, Press Play (via Lloud and RCA Records ). Directed by Grammy Award-winning filmmaker James Mackel, the visual is three-and-a-half minutes of spy stuff, our hero, dressed to impress, making short work of the many villains who lurk in her hotel. LISA is on the watch with a flight to catch, and has a job to complete.  She’s dressed for success as she leads a nifty choreographed routine with the hotel’s chambermaids and bellboys, and cooks up a flurry of punches, kicks and more en route to beating the stuffing out of the kitchenhands. “Got my nails really long like the barrel of my gun and my lipstick all over your face,” she sings, over the top of a sneaky beat. “I’m a boss, I’m a don when I’m driving to the sun. It’s a movie, baby, come and press play.” In the end, she gets a message through to her “favorite director,” who just happens to be in the building. Like a good Tarantino device, that red letter slipped under the door doesn’t give away its secret…

During the southern hemisphere spring, Andromeda is highest in the sky around midnight though. And in this telephoto scene from October 10/11, multiple exposures were used to reveal the spiral galaxy in tantalizing detail as it climbed above rolling Australian hills. Also known as M31 , the Andromeda Galaxy is one of the brightest objects in the Messier catalog , but is only visible to the unaided eye as a small, faint, fuzzy patch. items.title: YouTube’s latest trick lets you build a custom feed for every viewing mood
items.summary: YouTube is also giving its mobile homepage a makeover with a new top bar, with changes starting to roll out in the US.
items.body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR YouTube is redesigning its mobile app homepage with a simplified top bar, easier access to subscriptions, and new shortcuts for content categories. The headline feature is custom feeds, which let users create personalized recommendation feeds by describing a topic, content type, or mood. Users can save up to three custom feeds for free, while YouTube Premium subscribers can save up to eight. YouTube is refreshing its mobile app homepage to make it easier to switch between content categories and to give users greater control over their recommendations . The biggest addition is a new feature called “custom feeds,” which lets you build personalized video streams around anything you want to watch.

items.title: Nintendo Switch 2 jailbreak discovery could open the door to a world of mods
items.summary: An obscure game has provided an unlikely route into Nintendo's latest console.
items.body: Credit: Pepsipu.com TL;DR A developer has released a software-only Nintendo Switch 2 jailbreak that works on the latest firmware. The exploit uses vulnerabilities involving SmileBASIC 4 and has already been demonstrated with Mario Kart World mods. The jailbreak isn’t permanent and doesn’t yet provide full control over the console. Unsurprisingly, Nintendo hasn’t exactly made life easy for anyone hoping to tinker with the Switch 2 beyond its intended limits. But one developer has now made a significant breakthrough, releasing a software-only Switch 2 jailbreak that works even on the console’s latest firmware. Security researcher Sammy Hajhamid, who goes by pepsipu online, announced the achievement on X and explained how it works in a detailed blog post . The exploit, called ns2jb, works on firmware version 23.0.1 without requiring any physical modifications to the console. There are caveats, but the jailbreak may open the door to things like unofficial software and game modifications.

items.title: Samsung’s next big One UI update may be closer than you think
items.summary: A redesigned beta banner suggests preparations are already underway.
items.body: TL;DR Samsung has refreshed the One UI Beta Program banner in the Samsung Members app, potentially hinting at preparations for its next public beta. One UI 9.5 is already in internal testing, with previous leaks pointing to several potential new features. Samsung hasn’t confirmed a One UI 9.5 public beta launch date, but December is a possibility if it follows the One UI 8.5 timeline. Didn’t Samsung just finish the One UI 9 beta program? Apparently, there’s no rest for the software team or Galaxy owners eager to test what’s next. Barely a month after stable One UI 9 began rolling out to the Galaxy S26 series , Samsung is already dropping hints about its next big update. A redesigned banner in the Samsung Members app suggests the One UI 9.5 beta program could be warming up behind the scenes. As SamMobile reports, Samsung has refreshed the One UI Beta Program banner in the Samsung Members app, which Galaxy owners use to register for beta updates. The change is interesting because Samsung recently wrapped up its previous beta cycle, though the updated banner doesn’t explicitly mention One UI 9.5 or confirm that registration is about to open.

items.body: NASA, ESA, Michael Jones (California Institute of Technology); Image Processing: Gladys Kober (NASA/Catholic University of America) This NASA Hubble Space Telescope image released on Oct. 16, 2026, features the edge-on, intermediate spiral galaxy NGC 1827, located roughly 37 million light-years away in the constellation Columba, the Dove. Hubble captured the image as part of a survey looking at 260 satellite galaxies around 22 Milky Way-like host galaxies within a radius of about 32 million light-years from Earth. Low-mass galaxies like the ones in this Hubble observing program provide a way to test the predictions of cosmological models on small scales, which struggle to match observations. items.title: Some Android phones and Google Calendar events could soon be an hour off
items.summary: Android users in parts of Canada should check their phones before November 1.
items.body: TL;DR Parts of Canada are switching to permanent daylight saving time on November 1, ending seasonal clock changes. Google warns that Android phones running outdated software could incorrectly turn their clocks back by an hour. Some Google Calendar events could also shift by an hour, with certain appointments requiring manual corrections through the web version. The biannual tradition of changing clocks is coming to an end for a subset of the Canadian population, though with that convenience comes an added side of initial headaches. Permanent daylight saving time for British Columbia, Alberta, Manitoba, and the Northwest Territories starts on November 1, and with the date just a little over a week away at this point, Google wants to help Android users in those regions — or anyone traveling through them — make the transition. If the new rule hadn’t gone into effect, clocks in those regions would automatically turn back by an hour. Starting November 1, however, that won’t happen. While that sounds like a seamless transition, there’s a big catch here, especially for users who haven’t updated their Android devices.

items.title: Pebble OS is adding plugins to supercharge apps and watchfaces
items.summary: Pebble is making one of the biggest changes to its OS in recent memory.
items.body: Credit: Pebble TL;DR Eric Migicovsky has announced that Pebble OS will soon support plugins. The code is written in JavaScript and will run on smartphones rather than Pebble smartwatches. This update will allow watchfaces to provide data, like weather and stock prices, or perform actions without developers having to hardcode it in. It was only a week ago that a hands-on video showed us how the Pebble Round 2 compares to the Garmin Forerunner 165. Once again, Pebble is in the news, but this time it’s for the software. Pebble OS is getting one of its most significant updates in recent memory. According to founder Eric Migicovsky , the team is working on the “biggest change to the SDK since…forever.” The change in question refers to the addition of plugin support. This is a big deal for both developers and users alike. The reason why is that it will make apps and watchfaces far more versatile.

items.title: Google Meet expands real-time translation across 63 languages
items.summary: The feature detects and translates 63 languages.
items.body: TL;DR Google Meet just added Gemini-powered speech translation across 63 languages. The feature automatically detects spoken languages and translates them in audio and captions for individual participants. Real-time translation starts rolling out to some eligible users today. Meetings are meant to facilitate communication, but anyone who’s been in one that could have been an email, as the saying goes, knows that’s not always the case. That’s even more true for teams with multilingual members. Now Google Meet has a solution with Gemini-powered speech translation for 63 languages on web and mobile devices. In a new Workspace blog entry , Google shares that Meet users will be able to turn on speech translation for themselves in their preferred language at any point in a meeting using a dedicated translation control in the meeting toolbar. Google Meet will then automatically detect what language is being spoken and translate it for the user, both audibly and in captions. Google claims this translation takes place in “near real-time.”

items.title: 1Password’s new solution mitigates the security risks of AI agent account access
items.summary: 1Password just made giving your AI agent account access a little safer.
items.body: Credit: 1Password TL;DR 1Password has created a way for AI agents to use your passwords without actually seeing them. When an agent reaches a login screen, 1Password for Agents will autofill the password or one-time code so the agent can’t see or take possession of your credentials. It will work with a range of AI agents, such as Muse and Grok, with more to come later. You may trust an AI agent to help with your work, but you probably draw the line at letting it access your passwords. While understandable, that choice can also act as an obstacle when an AI agent needs access to an account. 1Password aims to solve the security risks of AI agent account access with its new solution. The digital vault and password manager company has announced 1Password for Agents. This new platform is designed to let AI agents use your passwords without letting the agent actually see or take possession of them. You’ll be able to connect it with Facebook’s Muse and SpaceX Super Intelligence’s Grok bot. More agent connections are expected to be on the way, including Claude Duet, ChatGPT Work and dots, Perplexity, and more.

items.title: Pour one out for Arc: One of the most hyped browsers is shutting down for good
items.summary: And we now know exactly when.
items.body: TL;DR The Browser Company has confirmed that Arc browser will shut down on December 22, 2026. New account registrations have already stopped, while Arc Search will lose its AI features and account syncing on November 23. Arc will stop working on Windows and macOS on December 22, and users can export their data before the shutdown. The writing has been on the wall for a while now, and it’s just been confirmed that one of the most hyped-up browsers is being shut down. The browser I’m talking about is Arc , and its days are numbered. We reported last year that The Browser Company had stopped active development on Arc to focus on an AI-first browser called Dia . Since then, Arc has been in maintenance mode, receiving only security updates and bug fixes. Now, the company is ready to take Arc off life support altogether, and we have a clear timeline of what’s happening next.

items.title: Your first look at the Galaxy S27 Ultra and Pro batteries is here, sort of
items.summary: The rumored Pro and Ultra have left another paper trail ahead of launch.
items.body: TL;DR Batteries believed to belong to the Galaxy S27 Ultra and S27 Pro have appeared in South Korea’s Safety Korea certification database. Earlier regulatory filings suggest the phones could feature 5,700mAh and 5,200mAh batteries, respectively. The batteries are pre-production units, and Samsung has not yet confirmed the phones’ final specifications. Is Samsung about to make a battery breakthrough with the Galaxy S27 series? We’ve heard rumors about everything from a massive 7,000mAh prototype for the Ultra to the possibility of silicon-carbon batteries . While the bigger battery dreams may not materialize, fresh certification photos have surfaced, giving us our first look at the batteries believed to be destined for the Galaxy S27 Ultra and its rumored Pro sibling. Notebookcheck spotted two batteries linked to the upcoming phones in South Korea’s Safety Korea certification database. They’re identified by model numbers EB-BS958DBY and EB-BS957CBY, under certification numbers YU10899-26034 and YU10899-26036, respectively. Both are manufactured by China-based Zhuhai CosMX Power Jinwan Subsidiary.

items.title: Google sounds like it’s had enough of the US renaming bodies of water
items.summary: After the Gulf of America and Lake America, Google resists rebranding the Atlantic.
items.body: TL;DR Over the past couple years, the US has been rejecting the established names of various bodies of water, renaming them after itself. Popular mapping apps like Google Maps have so far largely adopted those new names. Now Google CEO Sundar Pichai has reportedly drawn the line at efforts to rename the Atlantic Ocean. Things are weird right now in America. The current administration has expressed little interest in abiding by traditional norms, and that’s arguably no clearer than in its unprecedented efforts to rename international bodies of water with jingoistic “American” titles. While Google Maps has so far demonstrated nothing but willingness to deface its maps with the new names, it turns out that there may be one line it’s just not interested in crossing. Yesterday evening, reports The Washington Post , the president told a crowd in South Carolina that he asked Google CEO Sundar Pichai whether he’d be up to “handle” renaming the Atlantic Ocean.

items.title: Google Sheets is finally catching up to Excel with support for more chart types
items.summary: Box and whisker charts are finally here in Google Sheets.
items.body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR Google Sheets is rolling out support for box and whisker charts. If you select a range of numeric values, Sheets will calculate the minimum, first quartile, median, third quartile, maximum, mean, and outliers automatically without helper formulas. Box and whisker charts imported from Excel are now preserved, with data references, calculations, and formatting intact. Box and whisker charts are useful for displaying the distribution of data within a population. While they have long been a staple for Microsoft Excel, that hasn’t been the case for Google Sheets. However, Google is fixing that problem with a new update. Google Sheets is finally gaining native support for box and whisker charts. When you want to create one, you’ll just have to select a range of raw numeric values. Google says Sheets will automatically calculate the minimum, first quartile, median, third quartile, maximum, mean, and outliers for you. And best of all, you won’t need to use any helper formulas to accomplish this.

items.title: Put down your pitchforks — Google’s not hiding YouTube’s dislike button
items.summary: At least, not where it matters.
items.body: TL;DR YouTube users recently started reporting that they were finding their dislike button hidden away. Google now confirms that this change only appears for your own uploaded videos. Is there any relationship between a streaming service and its users that’s more contentious than YouTube’s? Even putting the interminable struggle between YouTube and ad blockers aside for the moment, it feels like nearly every single change the service makes to its interface is met with fierce pushback . Earlier this week, we told you about the newest controversy, as some viewers reported that the dislike button in videos was being hidden away , out of reach. As it turns out, this latest one might be no big deal, after all. As we shared at the time, impacted users observed that rather than finding the dislike button out in the open, perched right next to its like-button brother, YouTube was moving the the option behind a three-dot overflow menu — putting you one more tap removed from being able to dislike a video. It wasn’t the end of the world, but it did admittedly feel like YouTube was going out of its way to discourage negative feedback.

items.title: Google Chrome is done warning you about insecure websites after the fact
items.summary: The browser will now give you a heads-up before you visit an insecure website.
items.body: TL;DR Google is enabling Chrome’s “Always Use Secure Connections” setting for all users by default. Chrome will now warn users before connecting to insecure HTTP websites, giving them a chance to back out. Chrome won’t repeatedly warn users about approved HTTP sites, and Google says most users are unlikely to encounter these warnings anyway. An optional Chrome toggle that was first introduced back in 2022 is now being automatically enabled for everyone. Last year, Google announced its intention to make Chrome much safer for everyone , saying it would do so by prioritizing secure HTTPS connections when browsing the web and by warning users about websites still using the older HTTP protocol. Fast-forward to now, and Google is making good on that promise. The tech giant just confirmed that Chrome’s “Always Use Secure Connections” setting, which was enabled for users enrolled in Chrome’s Enhanced Protection mode of Safe Browsing earlier this year, has now become a standard part of the browsing experience.
